[b]Introduction :[/b]
Farming Simulator 22, développé par Giants Software et sorti en novembre 2021, c'est LA simulation agricole de référence. Des centaines d'engins sous licence, trois cartes, et pour la première fois dans la série : les saisons et les chaînes de production intégrées de base.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🌾 L'agriculture dans toute sa splendeur : des centaines de machines à conduire, des cultures variées (raisin, olives, sorgho en nouveauté), et des chaînes de production qui donnent enfin un vrai but à vos récoltes
[*]❄️ Le système de saisons enfin intégré nativement : déneigement au chasse-neige, gestion des animaux en hiver, serres... ça change complètement le rythme de jeu
[*]🚜 L'IA des ouvriers bien plus poussée qu'avant : on peut enfin déléguer les tâches ingrates et se concentrer sur ce qu'on aime faire
[*]🎮 Le cross-plateforme entre PC, PlayStation et Xbox : monter une ferme entre potes n'a jamais été aussi simple
[*]🧘 Ce côté zen incomparable : labourer un champ à 3h du matin en écoutant la radio, ça n'a pas de prix
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]📚 Toujours aussi rude pour les néophytes : les tutoriels expliquent le minimum et on se retrouve vite perdu entre les dizaines d'engins et de matériaux
[*]🚗 L'IA des automobilistes qui ne respecte rien et des ouvriers qui s'arrêtent parfois en plein champ sans raison
[*]🖥️ Techniquement daté : les textures des bâtiments, de la végétation et des PNJ manquent clairement de finesse
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
L'épisode le plus complet de la série, tout simplement. Les saisons et les chaînes de production apportent enfin la profondeur qui manquait, et le cross-play est un vrai plus pour jouer entre amis. C'est toujours aussi austère pour les débutants et techniquement en ♥♥♥♥♥♥, mais si vous cherchez une simulation agricole complète et relaxante, c'est celle-là qu'il faut prendre. Un bon cru.

[b]Note :[/b] ★★★★☆

Farming Simulator 22 is a great game, and after 352 hours, I can confidently say I've gotten a lot of enjoyment out of it. I really like pretty much every aspect of the game, but forestry has been one of my favorite parts. The realism is really well done without making the game feel unnecessarily complicated. There’s also a great variety of vehicles and equipment to use, and the maps offer plenty of options for different playstyles.

The mod support is another big plus, and I’ve enjoyed using a variety of mods to add even more to the game. Overall, I would definitely recommend Farming Simulator 22, especially if you enjoy simulation games or just want something relaxing to play. Honestly, after all the time I’ve put into it, there isn’t really anything I would change.

Farming Simulator 22 is a game I've spent a lot of time playing, and I can confidently say it's one of the best entries in the series. My journey with Farming Simulator started with Farming Simulator 17, then I moved on to 19, and finally 22. I haven't had the chance to play Farming Simulator 25 yet, but every game in the series has given me countless hours of enjoyment.

One of the biggest strengths of Farming Simulator 22 is the freedom it gives the player. You can build your farm however you like, choose the machines you want to use, decide what crops to grow, and expand at your own pace. The game never forces you into one specific playstyle, which is why it stays enjoyable even after many hours.

With every new Farming Simulator release, the developers introduce more licensed vehicles and equipment, giving players an even greater selection of machines to choose from. The DLCs are another huge advantage, adding new vehicles, equipment, and content that keep the gameplay fresh and exciting. Thanks to this, there's always something new to discover.

Another major highlight is the incredible modding community. Thousands of mods add new machinery, maps, buildings, and gameplay features, making the possibilities almost endless. It's thanks to the modding community that Farming Simulator 22 still feels fresh, even after spending countless hours in the game.

However, the most enjoyable experience for me was playing with the Logitech G Saitek Farm Sim Controller, which was designed specifically for Farming Simulator. Driving tractors, harvesters, and other agricultural machinery felt much more immersive with this setup. Whenever I played, I always tried to imagine that I was actually sitting behind the wheel of a real machine, and this controller made that feeling even stronger. Combined with its dedicated control panel, it genuinely felt like operating real farming equipment rather than simply playing a game.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that core physics and mechanics such as vehicle handling and driving feel dated and have not changed significantly from previous titles.

citations.review_text:
Rating: ★★★.7 (3.7/5)
As a huge fan of the franchise who has sank countless hours into it, Farming Simulator remains a great experience at its core. Taking care of livestock like cows, managing fields, and operating detailed machinery is deeply satisfying, and the overall graphical presentation keeps improving with each release.
However, despite my love for the game, it's hard to ignore where it falls short.
The most frustrating issue is that the underlying engine feels stuck in the past. The core driving mechanics and vehicle physics haven't meaningfully evolved since Farming Simulator 19—or even Farming Simulator 17. Fundamental physics like water interactions, vehicle handling, and realistic grain flow still feel dated. Furthermore, the stock maps feel surprisingly small and restrictive for a modern simulator, forcing heavy reliance on the modding community for large-scale farming.
It’s a great game, but after multiple entries, players shouldn't still be seeing so many legacy mechanics copy-pasted directly from older titles instead of getting a total physics overhaul.

citations.review_text:
Farming Simulator 22 is a pretty good game. 

Pros: There is more than one type of farming in this game. The feature where they will let you rent the train is pretty cool. The collectibles is pretty cool and can also help you earn money fast. You can change your outfit which i think is cool

Cons: The ai is pretty dumb, for example they will always try to cut me off and honk at me when there is nothing in front of them. I understand that in the real world, some drivers are not so smart. However, every ai driver is pretty dumb. The ai workers is also dumb because whenever there is two objects beside them, It will say the target is unreachable. the ai workers can also cause your game to crash and that happened to me. The ai cars for some reason act like they are glued to the ground. no matter how fast or hard you hit them, they will not move. Some vehicles are barley customizeable. Some dont even let you change the color of the vehicle. 

If you are thinking about getting this game, I think you should get the game. Many of the cons are pretty small and not that big of a deal.

This game is almost playable. It has so much potential. I have spent many hours setting up my ideal farm only to be blindsided by glitches. The game feels unfinished but they obviously have no plans to finish it as the developers have moved on to FS25.

Hay bales roll away at their own volition. AI workers drive my vehicles off cliffs, causing expensive damage and sometimes destroying a whole trailer load of goods. In constructing my coop I was able to place it in an area where the eggs were not accessible for pickup. There is no vehicle in which to transport my chickens therefore no way to move my coop. On top of this the save functionality is garbage - if you make a mistake such as buying a coop, it is set in stone because it will autosave on top of your save file when you open the quit menu. There is no save to revert to.

I have restarted many times, trying to avoid these pain points and enjoy the game - changing the focus of my farm, avoiding certain crops or types of animal. But I continue to encounter these unforeseen issues that take me out of the gameplay and remind me that this is just a poorly written computer game.

Presumably community mods would make this game more playable but I am so frustrated and unimpressed with the vanilla game I have no motivation to try. I don't have the energy to be hurt again. Fix FS22 before trying to sell me a new half finished game please.
